admin_cert.checked: Before it is accepted the pair is checked: the key matches the certificate, the term has begun and has not ended. On a refusal the previous pair stays in force. Your password is asked once more: whoever holds this certificate's key can read the admin UI's traffic.
admin_cert.config_only_html: No certificate, and admin_ui.uploaded_dir is empty: the pair is set in config.yaml only.
admin_cert.does_not_cover_html: It does not cover {0}, the name this page was opened with: the browser warns about it.
admin_cert.intro_html: The certificate this admin UI answers with — not the sites': theirs live on the domains page. The node neither issues nor renews certificates: it takes a ready pair, checks it and puts it in place. Nothing in config.yaml is changed here.
admin_cert.linked: The files are links — this is how certbot keeps its own. Renew with certbot: the admin UI takes the renewed pair up within 30 seconds. Replacing a link here would cut certbot's renewal off.
admin_cert.no_write: the node may not write next to {0}: replace the files on the machine, and the admin UI takes them up within 30 seconds
admin_cert.not_loaded: the pair was written and did not load: {0}
admin_cert.nowhere: there is nowhere to put the pair: admin_ui.uploaded_dir is empty
admin_cert.pending_html: A pair for {0}, valid until {1}, waits for the next start of the node.
admin_cert.self_signed: itself — a self-signed certificate, the browser warns
admin_cert.title: The admin UI's certificate
admin_cert.without_html: The admin UI works without a certificate, over plain HTTP — fine on loopback, behind ssh -L. A pair uploaded here lands in {0} and serves from the next start of the node: the listener that is already up cannot switch to HTTPS on the fly.
alerts.history_note: The history lives in the node's memory and starts anew with every restart of the core; every message is in the core's log as well.
alerts.intro_html: The node tells you when something is wrong with the site, without waiting for you to open this page. A trigger only tells: it changes neither the rules nor their mode. Each sends one message when it fires and one when things have been back to normal for a whole window; the message goes to the command set in alert delivery.
alerts.no_command_html: No command yet: the alerts go only to the core's log and to this page. Set one →
alerts.off_html: The alerts are off in the core's settings: alerts.enabled is false.
answer.blocked: not let through by the node
chart.columns_label: Requests over time by answer class
cloud.aggregates_text: Every fifteen minutes the node sends counters: network prefixes, client families, fingerprints, how many requests and how many were blocked. Never full addresses, User-Agent strings, paths, headers, cookies or bodies — the list of what never leaves is in the protocol, in the open repository, and it is the same document the cloud is built against. This is what makes the bases better for everybody, and it is how you will get an analysis of your own traffic later.
cloud.core_down: the core does not answer: the link to the cloud cannot be shown or changed
cloud.done_forgotten: The token is gone and both answers are cleared. The node talks to nobody.
cloud.done_registered: The node introduced itself to the cloud and took a token of the free level. Whatever you ticked is already in force — nothing needs restarting.
cloud.facts_text_html: Once a day the node fetches a signed set of facts: which networks belong to hosting providers, which addresses are a search engine's real crawler, which fingerprints belong to which browser. Facts only — what a client is called. What to do with such a client is decided by your rule and by nothing else: the cloud cannot switch a rule on here, and there is no method in the code that could. A set that is not signed by a key built into this binary is refused and the previous one stays in force.
cloud.forget_note: clears both answers; the node stops talking to the cloud and cannot resume without registering again
cloud.free_level: Ticking either one makes the node ask the cloud for a token of the free level — nothing to copy, nobody to write to. The free level gives the crawlers that Google, Bing, Apple and Yandex publish about themselves. Network classes, carriers whose ranges must never be blocked, proxy pools and fingerprints come with a subscription.
cloud.from_config_html: cloud.token is set in config.yaml, so the settings file decides and both directions are on. Whoever installed this node wrote it there by hand; this page does not override it.
cloud.in_config: this node's link to the cloud is set in config.yaml
cloud.known_as_note: call yourself this when you write to us
cloud.may_do: What this node may do with the cloud
cloud.no_set: no set applied: rules that refer to facts simply do not match, the rest work
cloud.token_none: none — the node talks to nobody
cloud.welcome_1: This node works on its own. It terminates TLS, fingerprints clients, applies your rules and writes events to disk — none of which needs us, and none of which sends anything anywhere.
cloud.welcome_2_html: Two things it can do with the cloud, and only if you say so here. Both are off until you tick them, and either can be turned off again on this page at any time.
cloud.welcome_title: Two questions, and then the node is yours
confirm.admin_certificate: Put this certificate on the admin UI? Whoever holds its key can read the admin UI's traffic.
confirm.alert_command: Save the alert command? It runs on this machine with the node's user.
confirm.crawlers_hold: Stop letting {0}'s crawlers past the rules? Their requests will go through the rules like any others.
confirm.crawlers_off: Turn the verified crawlers' pass off? Search engines, Google's checks and chat assistants will go through the rules like everyone, and a block written in a hurry may take the site out of the results.
confirm.forget_cloud: Forget the cloud token? The node stops talking to the cloud and has to register again to resume.
confirm.issue_token: Issue an API token? It outlives this session by months.
confirm.remove_domain: Remove {0}? The node stops serving it at once.
confirm.restart: Restart the core? Every site behind the node is cut off for a few seconds.
confirm.revoke_token: Revoke the token {0}? Programs that use it lose access at once.
confirm.title: Confirm with your password
confirm.to_active: Move {0} to active? From now on it acts on live traffic.
core.asked: The core was asked to restart. It finishes the requests in flight and stops; whoever supervises it — systemd or docker — starts it again within seconds. Reload this page to see the new start time.
core.down_html: The core does not answer. If it has stopped, its supervisor starts it again by itself; if it stays down, its log says why — journalctl -u antibot or docker logs.
core.intro: The core is the program that serves the sites: a process of its own, apart from this admin UI. The admin UI asks it over its control socket and has no other power over it.
core.restart_note: The core finishes the requests in flight and stops, and its supervisor starts it again. Every site behind the node is cut off for the seconds that takes. Your password is asked once more: a stolen session must not be enough to do that.
core.title: The core
crawlers.cloud_names_html: The cloud only sends who is a verified crawler; what to do with one is your decision here. The requests let through are in the events, marked verified crawler.
crawlers.held: held back — goes through the rules
crawlers.intro: A verified crawler is a network the fact set names a crawler's and marks "do not touch": the ranges search engines, Google's checks and chat assistants publish about themselves. The node lets such a request through before the rules, like your own networks — until you decide otherwise.
crawlers.named_only: named, not let past the rules
crawlers.no_facts: Not one request of this period has a network class: without a fact set there are no verified crawlers, and nobody to let through.
crawlers.no_file: No file for the decision (crawlers_file in admin.yaml): the pass cannot be changed from here.
crawlers.none_seen: Not one crawler from a verified network came over this period.
crawlers.owners_intro: Owners of crawler networks seen over the period. Collectors of training data are named but not verified: the cloud does not offer to let them past the rules, your rules decide.
crawlers.pass_is_off: Off: verified crawlers go through the rules like everyone.
crawlers.pass_is_on: On: verified crawlers pass before the rules, except those held back below.
crawlers.rules_intro: Only verified crawlers you held back, or all of them while the pass is off: the rest never reach the rules.
crawlers.through_rules: goes through the rules: the pass is off
delivery.config_language_html: The messages go in {0}: alerts.language is set in config.yaml and is changed only there.
delivery.core_down: The core does not answer: whether its settings name a command is unknown, nothing was changed
delivery.from_config_html: The command is set in config.yaml, in alerts.command, and is changed only there.
delivery.how_html: A shell command the node runs with its own user. The message arrives in $ANTIBOT_ALERT_TEXT and the other ANTIBOT_ALERT_* variables, and as JSON on stdin — never pasted into the command's text. Templates for Telegram, a webhook and mail are in the documentation, alerts.md. Your password is asked once more: the command runs on this machine.
delivery.in_config: The command is set in config.yaml and is changed only there
delivery.intro_html: Where the node sends its alerts. What fires and what has been sent is on the alerts page.
delivery.language_hint: Telegram, the webhook and mail get the messages in this language; the pages show them in the language of whoever looks.
delivery.no_command: No command yet: the alerts go only to the core's log and to this page.
delivery.nowhere_html: No place to keep a command: alerts.file is empty in the settings. The alerts are written to the core's log.
delivery.title: Delivery
domains.add_intro_html: The name clients come with, and the site's server the node forwards to — http://203.0.113.7:8080, or just 127.0.0.1:3000 for http. Loopback and private addresses are fine: the site often lives on the same machine. A pattern like *.example.ru covers every subdomain. The certificate is uploaded in the domain's row once it is added.
domains.fallback_html: Everything else — names no route knows — goes to {0}: the default route from the configuration. The DNS line is a hint: a domain that does not point at this machine never reaches the node.
domains.intro: Which names the node serves, where their sites live and which certificate each one answers with. Domains from the configuration file are shown but changed only there; domains added here go to their own file and take effect at once.
domains.no_certificate: No certificate — the node answers with its self-signed one, and the browser warns.
domains.no_renewal: The node neither issues nor renews certificates: renewal is uploading a fresh pair in the domain's row, or certbot next to the node.
error.core_down_unchanged: the core does not answer: nothing was changed
error.foreign_form: the request did not come from this page
error.upload_size: the upload was not accepted: two PEM files under a megabyte
events.latest_html: The last {0} events, newest first. Download every event matching these filters over the last day — the log's own lines, as NDJSON.
events.search: in the UA or the path
footer.note_html: antibot-admin {0} · rule conditions are composed with antibot rules; every change made here lands in the admin UI's log
header.core_down: The core does not answer on its control socket. Events, rules and domains are shown from their files and can be changed — the core takes the changes up when it is back. Alerts, the cloud and the certificates it serves are not shown until then.
login.accounts_html: Accounts are created with antibot admin passwd.

overview.cert_expires_in_html.other: The certificate for {1} expires in {0} days ({2}) — there is no auto-renewal; upload a fresh one on the Domains page or renew it with certbot.

overview.crawlers_intro: A self-declaration is a string anyone at all can put on themselves. A claim is confirmed only when the request came from a crawler network — the ranges crawler owners publish about themselves, delivered with the fact set. The rest nobody has checked: there an impostor and a real crawler look the same.
overview.crawlers_no_facts: No request here has a network class: without a fact set there is nothing to confirm a claim against.
overview.crawlers_tab_html: Whether verified crawlers pass before the rules — on the tab Rules → Verified crawlers.
overview.facts_only: The network class, its owner and the fingerprint family arrive with the fact sets — they change only what the client is called, and never what happens to it.
overview.not_fetched_html: not fetched: switched off in the cloud settings
overview.not_sent_html: not sent: switched off in the cloud settings
overview.talks_to_nobody_facts_html: This node talks to nobody: it has no token, and nothing leaves it — no aggregates, no requests for the bases. It works on the fact set applied from disk, version {0}. The two things it could do with the cloud, and what each of them sends, are in the cloud settings.
overview.talks_to_nobody_html: This node talks to nobody: it has no token, and nothing leaves it — no aggregates, no requests for the bases. The two things it could do with the cloud, and what each of them sends, are in the cloud settings.
overview.truncated: The variety of values hit the limit — the numbers in the breakdowns are incomplete.
overview.unknown: What the node does not know
overview.unknown_intro_html: While the network has no class and the fingerprint has no name, a rule has to be written blind: by the address and the User-Agent string, that is, by what the client says about itself.
overview.what_leaves: What leaves the node and what never does is written down in the documentation, protocol/aggregate.md: counts by five-minute windows, no addresses, no paths, no cookies.
proposals.accept_note: Accepted rules land in shadow: they only count until you move them to active on the Rules page.
proposals.advice_title: Advice about rules already at work
proposals.gone: there is no proposal or advice {0}
proposals.intro: For a paid analysis subscription the cloud looks at your own traffic and may propose a rule, or a piece of advice about one already at work. Nothing here does anything on its own — a proposal only adds a rule once you press Accept, and even then only into shadow.
proposals.not_a_proposal: this is advice, not a proposal — act on it with the rule's own buttons
proposals.reason_too_long: the reason is {0} characters long, the limit is {1}

rule.decided_or_marked: requests it decided or marked · {0} of all
rule.did_not_fire: It did not fire over the period.
rule.marked_in_shadow: requests it marked in shadow · {0} of all
rule.whom_html: Whom it touched is in the breakdowns below. A rule that touches a noticeable share of the requests almost certainly touches people too — that much traffic is never all bots; go through the addresses and fingerprints by hand before moving it to active. For a shadow rule the answers are what the site gave, that is, whom the rule would have cut off.
rules.advice_notice_html: The cloud has advice about this rule.
rules.intro_html: In the order of application: the first rule that fires in active mode wins. Observations (shadow) do not stop the walk. A rule can be enabled and disabled here, and moved between shadow and active; conditions are composed and edited with antibot rules.
rules.touches_people_html: A rule touching a noticeable share of the requests almost certainly touches people too: that much traffic is never all bots. To check whom exactly it will touch before turning it on — antibot replay.
tokens.days_nan: The number of days is not a number
tokens.intro_html: Tokens for the node's API — for a monitoring system, a panel of your own, a CI job that rolls rules out together with the site. A token is yours: it is issued only here or with antibot-admin api-token, and it never leaves for the cloud. A program sends it as Authorization: Bearer … to /api/v1/ on this address.
tokens.issued_html: Token {0} ({1}) — copy it now. The node keeps only its hash, and this page will not show it again.
tokens.log_note: Every issue and revocation lands in the admin UI's log with the name of the account; every change a token makes, with the name of the token.
tokens.name: name
tokens.scopes_html: read — the summary, the events and the list of rules; write — adding, switching and deleting rules as well. A monitoring token should only read: it must not be able to switch the protection off. Your password is asked once more: a token outlives the session by months.
